# Measurement-Free Memory Cost

This repository studies the internal non-Clifford processing needed to preserve
unknown quantum information through independent depolarizing noise. The complete
scientific account is organized by topic under science/.

Canonical entrypoints:
- README.md: question, principal bounds, reading routes, reproduction, scope,
  purpose and contact.
- science/model.md: authoritative operational model, noise convention, endpoints,
  Bell-fidelity and half-diamond conventions, exact claims and reading route.
- science/pauli_envelopes.md: binary support envelope, Clifford/reset updates,
  expected-rank contraction, replacement branches and diamond forgetting.
- science/control_cost.md: channel-rank and algebra bottlenecks, the 4^(-k)
  fidelity floor, gate-growth charges, logarithmic and exact discrete budgets,
  interval constraints and decoder-specific terminal rank.
- science/reliability_processing.md: absorbing Pauli-envelope updates, rank-dependent
  extinction hazard, first-extinction/Jensen cumulative-rank bound, specifically
  charged T-count consequence, score specialization and all-payload fixed-noise
  matching at width O(k+ln(D/epsilon)); primary attribution distinguishes the
  inherited complete-erasure/Jensen spacetime mechanism.
- science/guessing_processing.md: authoritative delayed-basis BB84 transfer,
  full-output CPTP quantum-plus-classical factorization, unconditional all-cut
  score floors, gate/interval corollaries and strongest inspected recovery
  comparison. Lattice-Memory-Certification supplies the finite guessing theorem.
- science/moment_processing.md: exponential-moment noise contraction, fixed
  averaged-channel recovery, direct score and recovery potential floors, finite
  gate/interval ledgers and fixed-score asymptotic converse.
- science/guessing_decay.md: finite inverse ledger retaining initial width,
  fixed-moment and stronger full-profile score-decay exponents, positive-rate threshold and
  certified optimization; a converse corollary, not achievable capacity.
- science/clifford_lifetime.md: finite random-stabilizer existence proof, noisy
  syndrome archive, exact chronology, full workspace accounting, final recovery
  and matching order of zero-T quantum lifetime.
- science/coherent_recovery.md: five-qubit syndrome polynomials, 42-T recovery
  node, concatenation, batching, finite parameters and upper resources.
- science/tanner_memory.md: inherited good Tanner-code decoder, fixed Boolean
  circuit and exact coherent compilation, prescribed T count, complete noisy
  workspace, current-syndrome residual invariant, correlated X/Z tails, code
  length availability, batching, fixed-level five-qubit extension to gamma<=1/20 and matching-order construction.
- science/interpretation.md: width and continuing work, catastrophic-reset
  baseline, endpoint/controller distinctions, matching regime and limitations.
- references/RELATED_WORK.md: primary attribution and operational comparisons.
- references/references.bib: structured primary-source bibliography.
- verification/README.md: finite checks, dependencies and their limitations.
- verification/run_all.py: deterministic suite and saved-output comparison.
- verification/Graph/README.md: Python-generated finite width/processing
  comparison, pinned dependencies, committed plots and numerical certificates.

Learning entrypoints:
- learning/report/Measurement_Free_Memory_Cost_Report.pdf: continuous self-contained explanation of the model, converse, constructions, matching-order regime and remaining physical questions.
- learning/source/README.md: technical build instructions for the explanatory report and its matching editable source.
- learning/README.md: project-specific route using the common Watrous (2018) anchor.
- learning/WATROUS_BRIDGE.md: selected Watrous sections, conventions, two-qubit
  algebra example, missing proof bridges and guessing-score application.
- learning/MILESTONES.md: exactly 30 learner-independent milestones (12 background, 18 innovation).

Reader routes:
- For a continuous explanation, read learning/report/Measurement_Free_Memory_Cost_Report.pdf.
- For the connected scientific account, read science/model.md and
  science/interpretation.md, then the relevant proof.
- For the converse, read science/pauli_envelopes.md followed by
  science/control_cost.md and science/reliability_processing.md.
- For an operational score premise, read science/guessing_processing.md after
  the model and algebra bottlenecks. The companion application is
  https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Lattice-Memory-Certification/blob/main/science/noisy-processing.md.
- For constructive storage, compare science/clifford_lifetime.md and
  science/coherent_recovery.md and science/tanner_memory.md
  under the same noise and endpoint convention.
- For a theorem, use its full proof and assumptions, not an introductory summary.
- For reproduction, follow verification/README.md and inspect the actual output.

Preserve these distinctions:
- gamma is the complete-depolarization mixing probability. Total nonidentity
  Pauli-error probability is 3*gamma/4; a record bit flips with probability gamma/2.
- D counts full noise rounds. Ideal processing between them can have arbitrary
  elementary depth; hardware gate-time claims require another model.
- Every persistent data, syndrome, controller and resource register is counted
  and noisy. There is no protected bypass or external classical decoder.
- Replacement states are independent of the retained memory and unknown input.
  A correlated external source retaining memory across times is not free.
- Actual surviving Pauli supports need not form a vector space. The proof uses
  a linear enclosure and may overestimate retained information.
- The main fidelity floor is a=2k*(1-epsilon-4^(-k))/(1-4^(-k)).
- The scalar injection optimum is a lower bound from necessary rank constraints,
  not an attained physical optimum for T-count.
- A general final decoder can have support rank much larger than 2k.
- Zero-T quantum storage uses exponential noisy width and defers nonlinear
  computation to unrestricted final recovery.
- The five-qubit coherent construction uses the standard code and exact
  seven-T Toffoli synthesis. Its six Toffoli-equivalent gates need no extra
  work qubits; their 42-T bound is not claimed optimal.
- The Tanner construction uses a fixed bounded-size local circuit with all
  minimizations, comparisons, ties and routing charged; scratch is reset on a
  fixed schedule and counted in n. The Gu et al. decoder/invariant and existing
  MFQEC mechanism are inherited. With a fixed number of inner five-qubit levels, for gamma<=1/20,
  n=O(k+ln(J/epsilon)), m_T=O(nJ), J=O(gamma D+1). It matches processing order
  for every payload at fixed positive gamma, D growing, epsilon bounded above
  below 1/2 and n=O(k+ln(D/epsilon)), by combining payload and reliability
  converses. This is not a sharp uniform weak-noise law. Constants can be enormous. The extended range is proved by constant-level composition,
  not inferred from an LDPC threshold; no coefficient is optimized.
- All constructions give half-diamond error epsilon. The converse assumes only
  Bell-overlap fidelity at least 1-epsilon.
- Measured QEC with noiseless external classical feedback is a different model.
  Do not claim that all QEC consumes magic or that fresh-state cost is T-count.
- For the guessing application, k counts independent BB84 challenge qubits;
  n counts every noisy persistent qubit; D counts full independent noise rounds.
  The device receives the quantum challenge alone. X is never revealed; only
  Theta arrives after all charged storage. The score is unconditional exact
  whole-string success, without postselection. Start one common full-output
  envelope at M=2n before any basis-dependent readout.
- Mathematical noise flags are independent channel choices used in the proof,
  not device information. Noisy counted controller records must also be
  processed through permitted charged primitives; arbitrary feedback is not free.
- Existing recovery inequalities reproduce the convenient mean-rank floors in
  science/guessing_processing.md. The moment chapter uses those recovery tools
  with the actual product-noise probabilities to strengthen the dynamical
  ledger. It does not claim a stronger pointwise guessing theorem or optimal
  physical cost. Its interval entry reserve bounds log_z E[z^r], not E[r];
  the full-output bound 2n is always safe. Neither route verifies device
  assumptions or imports an LWE processing wrapper.
- Watrous (2018) is the single educational anchor shared by both projects.
  Gottesman and other stabilizer sources remain primary scholarly references.
- The qualitative no-go result and stochastic Pauli framework are prior work.
  Complete-erasure/Jensen cumulative-spacetime reasoning is also prior work.
  The reliability extension adapts it to backward Pauli rank and specifically
  charged T/T-dagger processing with free Clifford/reset primitives. Zero must
  remain absorbing in every chosen envelope update.
- Finite checks establish their tested identities, not unrestricted asymptotic
  truth or external peer review.




Finite refinements: paired physical pivots give extinction hazard gamma^(r-s), with 2s the restricted symplectic rank. Keep the exact survival product and separate Bell/BB84 coherent-block floors, then retain exit rank in the T ledger. Zero-T negative moments give half-diamond forgetting at most 1-(1-q^D)^M. At fixed positive noise in the constructive range and error ceiling below 1/2, n_min=Theta_gamma(k+ln(D/epsilon)); the processing match is within a sufficiently large fixed factor of minimum width. None of these statements proves a uniform weak-noise or unrestricted width/work optimum.
